clue.text: One obligated to work for hire gets very small drink

parts.note: DR is the accounting abbreviation for debtor, someone under an obligation to pay
OP is short for opus, a musical or literary work
a property 'to let' is available for hire, so LET means for hire

explanation.surface: A hired hand on a tight budget is rewarded with only a tiny drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a labourer's meagre pay; really it is debtor, opus and the 'to let' sign strung together, with 'to' and 'gets' as links.
explanation.definitionFit: A droplet is a tiny drop of liquid, which makes a very small drink indeed.

clue.text: Seem much greater than some World War figures

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Certain leaders of the World Wars towered over everyone else.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwarf something is to make it look small by being far larger, so to seem much greater than it.

clue.text: Jealous husband to return greeting

indicators.note: to return the little word to means to read it backwards

parts.note: hello is an everyday greeting

explanation.surface: A suspicious husband comes back to say hi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to return' turns TO into OT.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Moor kills his wife Desdemona out of jealousy, making him the archetypal jealous husband.

clue.text: Tip a pound and French girl will drop English

parts.note: L, from Latin libra, is the abbreviation for a pound sterling
taken as written

indicators.note: to drop something is to let it go, so these words say a letter is removed from the French word

parts.note: fille is French for girl or daughter

explanation.surface: A French girl leaves a one-pound tip and loses her English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will drop' takes E (English) out of FILLE, leaving FILL. 'Tip' looks like a gratuity, but it is the British word for a rubbish dump.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a tip is a rubbish dump, and a landfill site is exactly that kind of place.

clue.text: Relief for poultry farmer at the end of the day: the smart know to cut cost, including call between setters and call to bull ring

definitions.text: Relief for poultry farmer at the end of the day

parts.note: taken as written
chic means stylish or smart
ken is Scottish and archaic for to know
to shave is to cut, as in shaving costs

indicators.note: including says the word cost wraps around the pieces that follow
between says the call sits with a setter on each side

parts.note: the crossword setter refers to himself as ME, so two setters give ME twice
ho is a call to attract attention
toro is the Spanish for bull, as called in the ring
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A long, rambling instruction about thrifty farmers, bird calls and bullfighting.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter calls himself ME, so 'setters' gives two of them; 'including' wraps the cost word round the calls. The definition reads the proverb literally: a farmer relieved that the birds are back in the coop at dusk.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says misdeeds return to haunt the doer; read literally, it is the evening relief of hens safely back in the henhouse.

clue.text: See 12
See 4
Disguise ourselves as queer and mad characters

indicators.note: characters are letters, here the letters of the preceding words used in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: We dress up in costume, pretending to be odd and crazy people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' signals that the letters of AS QUEER and MAD are rearranged; 'and' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Masquerade as a verb means to go about wearing a disguise or pretending to be someone else, so it fits a first-person plural use.

clue.text: Fellow too stringy?

definitions.meaning: a chap, addressed affectionately in old-fashioned British slang
a runner bean left too long on the plant becomes tough and fibrous

explanation.surface: A man so wiry he seems tough.
explanation.definitionFit: Old bean is a dated British form of address for a chap, and an over-ripe bean is literally stringy.

clue.text: "One shilling the box" — one given to mockery

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for shilling in old British money
a coffer is a strongbox or chest

explanation.surface: An advert prices a box at a shilling, and someone sneers.
explanation.walkthrough: A shilling was a pre-1971 British coin worth a twentieth of a pound; its abbreviation S comes from Latin solidus.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoffer is someone who mocks or jeers, a person given to mockery.

clue.text: Articles on a menu arranged by club

parts.note: A is the indefinite article
the is the definite article

indicators.note: arranged means the letters are set out in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The club's dining room sets items out on its menu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges A MENU into NAEUM; the two articles give A and THE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Athenaeum is a famous London gentlemen's club, and the word also names literary clubs generally.

clue.text: 16 across funny when the other way round

indicators.note: the other way round says the whole phrase is to be read backwards

parts.note: funny in the sense of strange, odd
as can mean when, as in 'as he arrived'

explanation.surface: A hermit seems amusing if you look at him from the other side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the other way round' turns the whole two-word phrase backwards, not each word separately; 'funny' means strange, not amusing.
explanation.definitionFit: A saddo is a pitiable loner with no social life, much like a recluse who shuns company.

clue.text: See 3
He's some — no, much — foot trouble; will he stand for it?

indicators.note: to trouble is to disturb, so these words are stirred up into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the S counting as a letter
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone with a nasty bout of foot trouble is asked whether he can bear to stand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges HE'S SOME NO MUCH FOOT. The definition pivots on 'stand for': a parliamentary candidate stands for a seat in the elected chamber.
explanation.definitionFit: British parliamentary candidates stand for election to the lower chamber at Westminster, so the elected house is what he stands for.

clue.text: Feast coming up as with other things after revolution

indicators.note: after says the next piece follows the previous one
in a down clue, coming up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
a revolution is a full turn
alia is Latin for other things, as in et alia

explanation.surface: A celebration rises again, with extra goings-on following an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' reverses the first little word, as befits a down clue; 'after' puts the Latin plural behind the turn; 'with' is a link. Saturn's feast was the Roman winter carnival.
explanation.definitionFit: The Saturnalia was the Roman midwinter feast of Saturn, a byword for riotous celebration.

clue.text: The law of little squares?

parts.note: the law given through Moses carries one name, and a picture made from many little square tiles carries the same word

explanation.definitionFit: Mosaic law is the law of Moses, and a mosaic is a picture built from small squares of stone or glass.

clue.text: One sails — with Silas, one's in

indicators.note: in says the numeral goes inside the surname

parts.note: Silas Marner is the weaver in George Eliot's novel, so Silas gives his surname
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone sets sail alongside Silas, joining the crew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's in' means one is in: I goes inside MARNER.
explanation.definitionFit: A mariner is a sailor, someone who sails the seas.

clue.text: About this: enter society for one who doesn't

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: enter says society goes into the word that follows

parts.note: the words being read are themselves a crossword clue

explanation.surface: Instructions on joining society, for someone who would rather not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this' self-referentially means this clue, CLUE; 'enter' puts S inside it. The definition 'one who doesn't' borrows 'enter society' from the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A recluse is someone who withdraws from the world and never enters society.

clue.text: Ethnic conflict with one painting church green coming up

parts.note: RA, a Royal Academician, is a painter elected to the Royal Academy
CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: raw means green, inexperienced

explanation.surface: Fighting breaks out as an artist gives the church a green coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' turns RAW into WAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A race war is a violent conflict between ethnic groups.

clue.text: One who finds excuses for everyone is among the players

indicators.note: among says the pieces sit inside the players

parts.note: the cast is the set of players in a show
U is the British film certificate for films suitable for everyone
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who makes excuses for all the actors is among them.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British film classification meaning suitable for all audiences.
explanation.definitionFit: A casuist uses clever but specious reasoning, especially to justify or excuse conduct.

clue.text: Fox had food so far

parts.note: tod is a dialect word for a fox
ate means had food

explanation.surface: A fox has eaten up to now.
explanation.definitionFit: To date means up until now, so far.

clue.text: Weapon free in temporary home

indicators.note: in says the word for free goes inside the shelter

parts.note: a tent is a temporary home
to rid is to free

explanation.surface: A weapon is released inside a camp.
explanation.definitionFit: A trident is a three-pronged spear, the weapon of Neptune and of Roman gladiators.

clue.text: Criminals returning so as to be split in opposing

indicators.note: split says the reversed pair is broken apart once it sits inside the word for opposing
in says the reversed pair goes inside the word for opposing

parts.note: contra means against, opposing

indicators.note: returning means the words so and as are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Lawbreakers go back so as to be divided among the opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' gives SAOS, and 'split' breaks it in two so the N of the word for opposing sits in its middle; 'to be' is a link. The Mafia's own name means 'our thing'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cosa Nostra is the Sicilian and American Mafia, a criminal organisation.

clue.text: Go round object of sowing to be 23-ed after …

definitions.meaning: to coil or turn around something

definitions.text: object of sowing to be 23-ed after
definitions.meaning: in Hosea, people sow this and reap the whirl-version of it later

explanation.surface: A tangled reference to sowing and later harvesting.
explanation.walkthrough: Hosea 8:7: 'they have sown the wind, and they shall reap the whirlwind'. The ellipsis carries on into 24-across.
explanation.definitionFit: To wind is to coil around; and the wind is what the biblical sinners sow.

clue.text: Stop some French potatoes

indicators.note: some says only part of the French phrase is used

parts.note: pommes de terre is French for potatoes

explanation.surface: Halt that batch of French spuds.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is hidden in the French translation, not in the clue's own words: pommes DE TERre.
explanation.definitionFit: To deter is to discourage or prevent, to stop someone acting.

clue.text: Cut with agent keeping his head

indicators.note: keeping means holding something inside

parts.note: a rep, or representative, acts as an agent
his refers back to the agent, whose head is the letter A

explanation.surface: A secret agent keeps his head while slicing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his head' is the first letter of 'agent', which REP holds inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To reap is to cut a crop such as corn.

clue.text: … round of activity when 4 5 down

definitions.meaning: a hectic bout of busy goings-on
what is reaped when misdeeds return, the first part of the biblical whirlwind following 21

explanation.surface: Busy times when the hens come home.
explanation.walkthrough: With 21-across this completes WHIRLWIND, the harvest of sowing the wind, which comes when the chickens come home to roost.
explanation.definitionFit: A whirl is a hectic round of activity, as in a social whirl.

clue.text: A sound people have time for making up

parts.note: a tone is a sound
men means people

explanation.surface: People find time for a reconciliation that sounds right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'have' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Atonement is making amends, making up for a wrong done.

clue.text: Return with one's steps to do another drawing

definitions.meaning: to go back the way one came
to trace a picture once more

explanation.surface: Going back the way you came to sketch again.
explanation.definitionFit: To retrace one's steps is to go back the same way, and to retrace a drawing is to trace it again.

clue.text: I can tell you who will win — keep it dark — there's a row about it

definitions.text: I can tell you who will win

indicators.note: about says the row goes round the call for silence

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
pst is a hiss for silence, asking someone to keep a secret

explanation.surface: A racing insider whispers a hot tip while an argument brews.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' looks like a quarrel but is a tier of seats. PST usually appears as psst.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipster offers predictions, typically in racing, telling punters who will win.
